Jordan / Soojin — forwarding Tom's questions (below). Drafting suggested language here so we can agree internally before sending to Acme. Please edit inline in the Drive doc if you want changes; I'll consolidate for Tom.

Suggested SLO / measurement bullets (draft)
- Latency measurement: For Hosted API, latency is measured end-to-end from Redwood's public ingestion edge to the time the final token is emitted by Redwood's runtime (p50/p95/p99 reported). For Private deployments (customer-hosted), Redwood measures from Redwood agent ingress to final token; network transit inside the customer's VPC is excluded from our measured latency.
- Streaming-specific metrics: Time-to-first-token is measured as time from request ingestion to the first token emitted. Tail latency is p95/p99 of the final token. We will report both metrics separately for streaming workloads.
- Throughput and concurrency: We will define sustained throughput as the average rps over a 5-minute sliding window. Burst capacity is measured as maximum sustainable rps over a 30s window; concurrency is measured as concurrent active sessions hitting the model.
- Reporting cadence and remedies: Monthly SLO reports with dashboard access. Remedies will be service credits applied to the next invoice for monthly SLO misses, with an escalation row for repeat misses (>=3 months in a rolling 6 month window). Exclusions will include scheduled maintenance with 72h notice, force majeure, and customer misconfiguration or third-party outages.

Notes for Jordan: aligning on wording for "ingress point" and the customer-network exclusion text is important — legal will want the customer-facing phrasing to be unambiguous. Also need a short paragraph for the procurement-facing one-pager that lists measurement windows and how we handle partial-month POC prorations.

Attachments: redwood-slo-draft-v1.docx, throughput-worksheet.csv

Thanks —
Karthik
